speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) with Pancoast syndrome. The patient's history of smoking, progressive right arm weakness, decreased sensation, significant weight loss, and diabetes (risk factor for neuropathy, but the focal upper extremity symptoms suggest a structural mass) are highly suggestive of an apical lung tumor compressing the brachial plexus and sympathetic chain. I recommend a Chest X-ray and MRI of the thoracic inlet for confirmation.
